transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2025-12-18
- Start: 15:00 PST
- Duration: ~58 minutes
- Recording: enabled
- Notes: Console walkthrough focused on usage analytics, per-route dashboards, cost breakdown, and reserved capacity options.

Summary:
Maya opened with a one-line agenda: show the Console per-route views, how token-level chargeback works, and what committed routes would look like for Skyline's ingestion + analytics workloads. Customer is concerned about spiky traffic (batch vs realtime), per-route cost attribution, and data residency/SOC2. Diego to follow up with VPC/SOC docs.

Topics discussed (auto): usage analytics, route grouping, cost attribution, reserved routes, burst/overage policies, SOC2/VPC, billing CSV, demo links.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh I think we have about an hour. i'll do a quick console walkthrough and diego will chime in where we get into infra and vpc stuff.
[00:12] Jordan Blake: thanks, Maya. quick note, Aisha's connection might pop in and out so if audio goes weird, call it out.
[00:17] Aisha Khan: yep, i'm here — audio fine.
[00:23] Maya Chen: great. ok i'm sharing my screen — can you see the Redwood Console?
[00:28] Tommy Lee: yes, seeing it. UI looks familiar from the docs.
[00:31] Maya Chen: cool. first panel is the global usage overview, token trends, top models. for Skyline i'd expect most traffic to be on two routes: "ingest-normalize" and "insight-query" based on what Jordan described earlier.
[00:42] [00:45] Diego Alvarez: quick mic note, sometimes the auto transcription says KV cache as K V cass — ignore that, we call out KV cache in the docs.
[00:50] Maya Chen: thanks. ok zooming into routes — here is per-route dashboard. you can see requests per minute, p50/p95 latency, and token breakdown per route. note the chart on the right: "cost per route" — that's token cost + model footprint + optional quantization overhead.
[01:12] Jordan Blake: curious how that's calculated. is that the billed number or an estimated internal cost?
[01:17] Maya Chen: good question. so the Console shows two columns: "Invoice view" (what the hosted billing would show) and "Unit economics" (our estimated cost back to you based on GPU time, occupancy, and batching efficiency). the unit economics is what our optimize engine recommends changes against.
[01:37] Aisha Khan: when you say batching efficiency, does that assume a certain tail-latency SLO? our SRE team is very sensitive to p99 spikes.
[01:45] Diego Alvarez: yes — the optimizer uses your configured SLO; you can set a latency target per route and the optimizer will recommend batch sizes and quantization that keep p99 under that threshold while minimizing cost. it simulates throughput to produce the recommendations.
[02:05] Tommy Lee: can the dashboard show baselines over a custom window? we want to attribute cost to product teams monthly.
[02:11] Maya Chen: absolutely, date range selector at top, and you can group by route tags — we also support cost allocation tags so you can map routes to billing owners. we'll demo exporting a billing CSV in a sec.
[02:23] [02:30] Jordan Blake: also, do you persist token-level logs? data residency and retention are a big thing for us.
[02:35] Diego Alvarez: on hosted, we retain minimal telemetry for 30 days by default and you can extend retention. for Private/VPC installs you control retention — tokens are not stored unless you enable request logging; we redact prompt data by default in telemetry. we can attach the SOC2 and data flow diagrams to your ticket.
[02:54] Maya Chen: moving on to the cost breakdown view — here's a per-route breakdown that decomposes cost into model compute, batching overhead, cache hits, and network egress. see how cache-hit rate dramatically reduces incremental token compute?
[03:10] Aisha Khan: that cache number — is that the prefix cache or KV cache?
[03:14] Diego Alvarez: both — we surface prefix caching and KV cache separately; KV cache savings appear in generation-side token counts because they avoid re-computation of cached KV states.
[03:26] [03:30] Tommy Lee: the graphs are helpful. is the "model compute" column normalized per-1000 tokens?
[03:35] Maya Chen: it's normalized to your configured units, default is cost per-1k tokens, yes. you can switch to per-invocation or per-hour view.
[03:42] Jordan Blake: we run mixed workloads — some heavy embeddings, some chat. can we group routes by model family and see combined cost?
[03:48] Maya Chen: yes, use the grouping options — group by model tag, team, or route label. the console supports cross-filtering, so selecting the model family will highlight routes that use it.
[04:00] [04:05] Diego Alvarez: quick aside — if you plan to move to Dedicated, the Console will still present the same metrics; the difference is some of the unit economics will flip because you have reserved GPU cost amortization.
[04:16] Aisha Khan: about Reserved routes — what's the commitment shape? monthly v annual? how do bursts get handled?
[04:23] Maya Chen: reserved routes are committed capacity for a route or route group. typically monthly or annual SKUs. bursts are allowed up to a configured burst buffer; beyond that, requests fall back per your policy — you can choose queued, degrade to smaller model, or fail.
[04:39] Tommy Lee: can we set fallback to our slower on-prem model if Redwood capacity is limited?
[04:42] Diego Alvarez: yes, that's supported via routing policies — you can chain endpoints, Redwood will failover to an onboarded private endpoint or to a smaller hosted model.
[04:52] [05:00] Jordan Blake: do you have examples of cost savings from batching and caching? any benchmark we can look at?
[05:05] Maya Chen: yes, we ran a public benchmark on a QA workload and saw up to 3.8x token-cost reduction using batching + KV cache on steady workloads. i'll attach the benchmark spreadsheet.
[05:16] Aisha Khan: please send that. also, does the Console show predicted spend for next month? we'd like forecasts.
[05:23] Maya Chen: Forecasting tab uses historical trend + seasonality; you can override assumptions like expected daily traffic growth. forecasts are per-route and aggregate.
[05:32] [05:45] Tommy Lee: i noticed an "optimize" suggestion panel — does that run continuously?
[05:48] Priya Rao: (joined) hey all, Priya here — the Optimize engine runs in two modes: continuous monitoring with lightweight suggestions, and periodic batch analysis that produces recommended quantization and batching profiles. you can choose auto-apply or manual review.
[06:05] Jordan Blake: any risks with auto-apply? like a quality regression?
[06:09] Priya Rao: we tie optimize suggestions to prompt sets and have a regression monitor. any auto-apply can be gated behind canary rollouts; you can set a quality threshold and if regressions exceed it we automatically roll back.
[06:22] [06:30] Aisha Khan: that's reassuring. can you show the alerting on quality regressions?
[06:33] Maya Chen: sure — in the Console there is an alerts section. here's an example where a quantization change bumped a rouge metric on a prompt set, and Console created an alert with diffing and linked examples. you can integrate with PagerDuty or Slack.
[06:50] Tommy Lee: about billing exports, can we receive a line-item CSV that maps each invocation to route, customer tag, tokens, model, and unit price?
[06:58] Maya Chen: yes — export > billing CSV includes those fields. we also provide a pivot-ready sheet that translates to per-team chargebacks and includes amortized Dedicated costs. i'll attach a sample.
[07:14] Jordan Blake: for Private deployments, how are invoices handled? is it a license plus usage?
[07:20] Diego Alvarez: Private is typically an enterprise license fee + optional usage-based add-on depending on how you run inference (we can structure it as committed nodes + overage). we can map it in the pricing doc.
[07:33] [07:40] Aisha Khan: any SSO/SAML controls we can preview? we need role-based access for ops vs data scientists.
[07:45] Maya Chen: yes, SSO with SAML and OIDC is supported, plus RBAC roles. Console audit logs show user activity and route changes; we feed those into your SIEM if desired.
[07:58] Tommy Lee: great. are there per-token redaction flags for PII? we want to keep user prompts out of logs.
[08:03] Diego Alvarez: by default we PII-redact certain fields and you can opt into full request logging for debugging, but that's tenant controlled; keys and KMS are integrated for Private deployments.
[08:20] [08:30] Jordan Blake: maybe we should talk expected volumes — to see savings. our two routes are roughly 1.8M tokens/day peak bursts to 5–6M on some days.
[08:40] Maya Chen: ok — with numbers like that we can run a quick model: at hosted on-demand pricing, that traffic ballparks to approx $X/day; with reserved routes and batching you could cut the unit cost by ~30–50% depending on cache hit rate. i'll produce a concrete sample in the pricing sheet.
[08:58] Aisha Khan: can you also show how to tag routes so our billing system can import?
[09:03] Maya Chen: sure — route config -> metadata tags. i'll add a short demo of route-level tags mapping to your internal cost center codes.
[09:15] [09:30] Tommy Lee: one more on observability: do we get traces for calls and can we correlate them to model comp time?
[09:36] Priya Rao: yes — trace IDs are in each request and Console shows end-to-end timing: client->ingress->model->egress. you can filter traces by route and latency bucket.
[09:50] Jordan Blake: nice. ok, i'd like to see the sample billing export and the reserved-route pricing.
[09:55] Maya Chen: noted. Diego, show the VPC diagram?
[10:00] [10:05] Diego Alvarez: sharing my screen now — here is a VPC peering pattern we use for Private customers, with optional customer-managed NAT. we also show HSM/KMS integrations for key rotation.
[10:20] Aisha Khan: the network egress path — can you limit egress to only our analytics subnet?
[10:25] Diego Alvarez: yes — with Private we can lock down to your subnets. hosted options have region-specific egress controls and egress logs.
[10:36] [10:45] Tommy Lee: what about audit log retention? we need seven years for compliance.
[10:50] Diego Alvarez: for enterprise Private customers we offer configurable retention and long-term storage hooks to your S3. we'll scope that in the SOW.
[11:02] Jordan Blake: excellent. on a tactical note — can you drop links to the Console demo and the sample spreadsheet in the meeting notes?
[11:08] Maya Chen: yes. sending in chat now — Console demo: https://redwood.example/demo/console/skyline-sample (demo link), Benchmark sheet: https://redwood.example/benchmarks/batching-kv-2025.xlsx, Billing sample: https://redwood.example/samples/billing-sample.csv.
[11:26] [11:40] Aisha Khan: i clicked the demo — looks good. question: for forecast, can we produce a "conservative" and "optimistic" scenario?
[11:48] Maya Chen: yes, forecasting supports scenario presets. we'll include those in the export.
[11:55] Tommy Lee: about integration — is there a webhook when a route crosses a spend threshold? we want to automate alerts.
[12:01] Priya Rao: yep— alerting supports webhooks, slack, and custom integrations. you can set route-level thresholds on estimated spend or absolute token volume.
[12:10] Jordan Blake: any known limitations on the console if we bring a private model (on-prem) into the control plane?
[12:16] Diego Alvarez: you can onboard private endpoints; some telemetry will be sampled for privacy but we retain key metrics. we'll discuss sampling policy for your SOW.
[12:29] [12:40] Maya Chen: we're about halfway, any other burning questions?
[12:44] Tommy Lee: just curious about error budgets for reserved routes, like what happens when committed capacity is exhausted multiple times in a month?
[12:52] Maya Chen: we have an SLA-backed remediation playbook; overages are billed at a defined rate but we flag repeated breaches and offer capacity rescheduling or credits depending on root cause.
[13:05] [13:20] Aisha Khan: ok, sounds good. Jordan — are you comfortable with next steps?
[13:25] Jordan Blake: yes. let's get the pricing sheet and SOC2 artifacts, and then schedule the private-deploy scoping.
[13:31] Maya Chen: perfect. quick recap of action items...
[13:35] [14:00] Closing notes:
- Maya to send pricing + billing sample + benchmark sheet (Maya)
- Diego to attach VPC and SOC2 excerpts (Diego)
- Priya to run baseline perf on Skyline prompt set after they send sample prompts (Priya)

End-of-transcript.
